This isn’t a new trend; sales of new cars are on pace to decline for the fifth straight year, and Detroit’s two largest automakers are reportedly taking action. Per a report from The Wall Street Journal, GM plans to stop production of the Chevrolet Sonic as early as this year as well as the Chevrolet Impala over the next few years. GM’s crosstown rival, Ford, is planning similar moves and will stop producing the Fiesta for the U.S. market as soon as 2019, and will also chop the Taurus — a nameplate that was once Ford’s flagship sedan in the U.S. market. These moves have been considered for some time; Fiat Chrysler Automobiles (NYSE:FCAU) already axed the Dodge Dart and Chrysler 200 from its U.S. portfolio, so it could push all-in on more profitable Ram Truck and Jeep brand sales, which are far more lucrative.
